quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do woven fabrics and knitted fabrics differ in the way yarns are assembled, and how does that structure affect the fabric's behavior?
quiz_item.question: How do woven fabrics and knitted fabrics differ in the way yarns are assembled, and how does that structure affect the fabric's behavior?
options: A. Woven fabrics are fused directly from loose fibers using heat and glue, whereas knitted fabrics are spun without yarn.

B. Woven fabrics interlace two perpendicular sets of yarn (warp and weft) on a loom to create a firm, stable cloth, whereas knitted fabrics interlock loops of yarn to create a flexible, stretchy material.
C. Woven fabrics can only be made from synthetic polyester, whereas knitted fabrics can only be made from natural sheep wool.
D. Knitted fabrics have zero elasticity and unravel only when cut with pinking shears, whereas woven fabrics stretch easily in every direction.

quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Weaving crosses lengthwise warp yarns and crosswise weft yarns at right angles for dimensional stability, while knitting forms interlocking loops that give garments natural stretch and recovery.

Step 4 - Untwist and Snap the Yarn: Hold the ends in your fingers and pull the yarn apart (p. 27).

quiz_item.question: When comparing fiber categories and ecological impacts, which statement accurately reflects a trade-off between natural and synthetic fibers?

B. Natural fibers are comfortable and absorbent but wrinkle or shrink more easily, while synthetics offer high strength and wrinkle resistance but rely on nonrenewable petrochemicals
C. Natural animal fibers like wool cannot be dyed and are completely fireproof at any temperature
D. Cellulosic fibers require zero water or chemicals during wood-pulp processing
choices: A. Synthetic fibers biodegrade in soil within days, whereas natural plant fibers never decompose
B. Natural fibers are comfortable and absorbent but wrinkle or shrink more easily, while synthetics offer high strength and wrinkle resistance but rely on nonrenewable petrochemicals

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do woven fabrics and knitted fabrics differ in the way yarns are assembled, and how does that structure affect the fabric's behavior?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do woven fabrics and knitted fabrics differ in the way yarns are assembled, and how does that structure affect the fabric's behavior?
options: A. Woven fabrics are fused directly from loose fibers using heat and glue, whereas knitted fabrics are spun without yarn.

B. Woven fabrics interlace two perpendicular sets of yarn (warp and weft) on a loom to create a firm, stable cloth, whereas knitted fabrics interlock loops of yarn to create a flexible, stretchy material.
C. Woven fabrics can only be made from synthetic polyester, whereas knitted fabrics can only be made from natural sheep wool.
D. Knitted fabrics have zero elasticity and unravel only when cut with pinking shears, whereas woven fabrics stretch easily in every direction.
choices: A. Woven fabrics are fused directly from loose fibers using heat and glue, whereas knitted fabrics are spun without yarn.

B. Woven fabrics interlace two perpendicular sets of yarn (warp and weft) on a loom to create a firm, stable cloth, whereas knitted fabrics interlock loops of yarn to create a flexible, stretchy material.
C. Woven fabrics can only be made from synthetic polyester, whereas knitted fabrics can only be made from natural sheep wool.
D. Knitted fabrics have zero elasticity and unravel only when cut with pinking shears, whereas woven fabrics stretch easily in every direction.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Woven fabrics interlace two perpendicular sets of yarn (warp and weft) on a loom to create a firm, stable cloth, whereas knitted fabrics interlock loops of yarn to create a flexible, stretchy material.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Weaving crosses lengthwise warp yarns and crosswise weft yarns at right angles for dimensional stability, while knitting forms interlocking loops that give garments natural stretch and recovery.
